deals.headline: 49ers Enterprises buys 15% of Leeds United
deals.summary: 49ers Enterprises became a minority investor, buying 15% of the club from majority owner Andrea Radrizzani; Paraag Marathe joined the board.

deals.evidence: bringing the total minority ownership stake in Leeds United managed by 49ers Enterprises to 37%
deals.headline: 49ers Enterprises raises Leeds United stake to 37%
deals.summary: A new investment by a 49ers-affiliated entity brought the total minority stake managed by 49ers Enterprises to 37%; Paraag Marathe became vice chairman.

deals.evidence: Leeds United are now owned by 49ers Enterprises after the English Football League formally approved their £170m takeover of the Championship club.
deals.headline: EFL approves £170m 49ers Enterprises takeover of Leeds United
deals.summary: The EFL approved 49ers Enterprises' takeover, ending Andrea Radrizzani's ownership; Radrizzani's stake had reduced to 56% by the time he sold. BBC reports the takeover at £170m; the club did not state a price.

deals.summary: Red Bull took a minority ownership stake in Leeds United and became front-of-shirt sponsor; no stake size or price was stated.

deals.headline: Owners inject £108m into Leeds United
deals.summary: Money from the 49ers Enterprises ownership group was used to pay down underlying debt and fund transfers and wages; cash from investors totalled £108m in the 2024-25 accounts.

Companies House PSC on Leeds United Football Club Limited (06233875): John Edward York and Paraag Vijay Marathe, significant influence or control, notified 25 September 2023. Shirt sponsor not recorded: Leeds Live names SBOTOP as front-of-shirt sponsor for 2024/25 while BBC (May 2024) says Red Bull would take over front-of-shirt; current sponsor not confirmed. Elland Road capacity 37,890 is from The Sporting News 2025/26 table via Yahoo Sports. Forbes' Leeds page carries a 2022 value ($800m), so Sportico 2026 ($680m) is used. ownership_summary: Owned by 49ers Enterprises, the investment arm of the NFL's San Francisco 49ers (York family, led by Jed York and president Paraag Marathe), which took full ownership on 17 July 2023 after EFL approval of a reported £170m takeover from Andrea Radrizzani; it first bought 15% in 2018 and reached 37% in January 2021. The syndicate includes individual investors (Russell Crowe, Will Ferrell, Jordan Spieth, Justin Thomas, per BBC) and, since May 2024, Red Bull as a minority shareholder. Companies House lists John York and Paraag Marathe as persons with significant influence or control.
